I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea.

Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: The user says: "I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee". They want us to log these foods. We have a tool to log food items. We need to call the function for each food item. The user didn't specify portion amounts for the tea or coffee. We can assume default portion amounts? The function requires portion_amount: number. We need to provide a numeric portion_amount. For tea and coffee, we might assume 1 cup. For frozen mango, they said 8 pieces. So portion_amount=8, portion_unit="piece". For pepperoni pizza, 2 slices. So portion_amount=2, portion_unit="slice". For chai tea, 1 cup. For coffee, 1 cup. We also need to specify meal_type. The user didn't specify meal times. We can default to snack. Or we can guess: maybe the earlier items were lunch? But we don't know. We can default to snack. The log_date: we can use current date/time. We can use ISO 8601. Let's use something like "2026-06-01T12:00:00Z" for earlier items, and "2026-06-01T15:00:00Z" for later items. But we don't know times. We can just set log_date to null or default. The function default for log_date is null. So we can omit it. We'll call the function for each item.
